The admissible evidence supports launch readiness at an aggregate level, which is the best available basis for certification. But the same admissible record directly undercuts a clean certification posture: a named launch context lacks evaluation coverage, current checks exclude it, QA treats the gap as unknown, and policy requires disclosure or approved risk acceptance before clean certification. That makes the defense of certification without deployment limitation weak. The most defensible packet is therefore one that certifies while precisely characterizing the basis as aggregate readiness plus general operational checks, and explicitly acknowledges that the record is thin on the named-context issue.
